utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Popovic. Just a couple of questions, a couple of points remaining to be clarified. First of all, in connection with the last issues broached by the Prosecutor, do you remember, during the military administration, so we're talking about the end of July 1992, which body was there in Samac: The Crisis Staff or the War Presidency, formally?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor quoted sections of Simo Zaric's statement. According to your personal information and knowledge, in cases of looting or wherever looting has been ascertained, who was in charge of starting the procedure?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military security and civilian security were in charge of that, whenever they had knowledge of any such thing, they would automatically have to take action to stop or prevent looting. If there was organised looting and if they had information that there was organised looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, do you remember an order by General Talic on introducing the military administration from July 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the oral part, but I've never seen it in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about your personal knowledge about that. The military administration, were they in charge of property in the area of the military administration and the republic stock and supplies? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were rules and instructions then, and it was up to the military administration and the army to organise for facilities to be guarded, for goods to be transported, and certain instructions were issued pursuant to which a person could move about within the area of responsibility of the Tactical Group. Therefore, it is clear from this that someone failed to do their job, or something along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just another question issuing from the line of questioning by the Prosecutor. Do you remember to what extent Simo Zaric really spent time? How much time he really spent in Odzak? Because the military administration continued until 1993. Can you remember how much time Simo Zaric actually spent at the council of the military administration?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was only there very briefly. I couldn't specify whether it was for a month or longer, but I think certainly very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Popovic, the Prosecutor asked you about the figures concerning the Serbian and non-Serbian population. Now, after Dayton, how many Serbs are there in the area of Odzak municipality?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dozens, perhaps, a hundred possibly. I'm not sure, but not too many.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit P169, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovic, this morning you were asked by the Prosecution about several issues concerning the dispatch by the Tactical Group 1, dated 12 May 1993, signed by Colonel Ratomir Simic, about a meeting that was held at the military administration. I will read this to you. I don't know whether you can see on the screen the first page of this document, and then if you can tell me, please, whether you remember that. So on page 1 of the dispatch, item 1 of the agenda was preserving property in the area of TG 1 from being taken away and taken out of the area. Under 2: What to do with the property that is currently under protection but should be given to the goods, supplies, and stocks. Number 3: Monitor the situation and solve all major problems, if any, the case of the silos. List and record the property and the like. Item 4: The situation of the military administration and the decision regarding the cessation of military administration. Mr. Popovic, I know it's been more than ten years, or actually, almost ten years since the meeting we are now talking about. These four items of the agenda, do they reflect the issues that were actually debated at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I couldn't remember this meeting, that this meeting ever took place, but by looking at this dispatch, I see that there was indeed such a meeting. And I think this was more or less what was present on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you turn to page 2 of the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 2 of Colonel Ratomir Simic's report, to his Superior Command, the 1st Krajina Corps, the report claims that Mr. Blagoje Simic, the president of the Samac SO, so this is the Municipal Assembly of Samac, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He proposed for the military administration to be abolished as soon as possible. He provided the example of a farm where cows were kept for milking. He said that the military administration had taken away several lorries of leather and no one knew where they had taken the leather to. Do you remember Mr. Simic discussing that at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to think back, and I know that when Colonel Simic came and when Todorovic was in charge of civilian affairs, the council became less important, that that man took over everything. So no wonder that there were cases of misappropriation of property. You've just referred to the case of cows and leather being taken away. That's exactly what started happening when the colonel came and his deputy, Todorovic. And then a month later, I think, another colonel was brought in, who was not a member of the command but rather -- who was not at the command, at the command building, but rather in a different building, where the council was. He only stayed for a very brief while, and then that whatever its name is, military administration was reintroduced and then Colonel Milivoje Simic came. This was all strange, the way things developed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you refer to Todorovic, who was in charge of civilian affairs, do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So this is not Stevan Todorovic, chief of police in Samac that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a man who came with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Mr. Ratomir Simic, the commander, he brought him and he appointed him commander for civilian affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On page 2, which you may be looking at - this is an exhibit tendered by the Prosecution today - Colonel Simic proceeds saying that the president of the municipality would like to say the following. This is towards the bottom of the page. I'll read this out to you. He said that every army keeps doing in its own sector whatever it likes, that the army is a state institution, and that he, Dr. Simic, as the president of the Municipal Assembly, cannot accept contact with local commanders. He goes on to say: There is a government, there is a main staff. So that's where these things should be dealt with. Do you remember that particular section referred to by Dr. Simic at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in which context this discussion was held. If he told me probably that there was a bit of misunderstanding between the commands of the tactical groups in relation to the civilian population, because we had the return of the refugees, not the refugees, but rather the arrival of the refugees in the area of Odzak municipality, and the return of our people, who were coming, who were voicing their discontent. And then when this man came, the man I've just told you about, and the change probably, that's when this conversation ensued, the conversation between the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, last question related to this document: There is a reference to two other names here. Do you remember at that meeting, was General Bogdan Subotic also present, who was also the minister of defence in the government of Republika Srpska at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I can't remember that it was a general. Somehow this doesn't ring a bell. I don't think I've ever seen that man. I have heard of Subotic. Now, whether he was present or not, I really can't answer that. I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On page 1 of this document - I'm not sure if you can see it - we discussed this this morning. There are the names of the participants. Number 7, minister of justice of the government of Republika Srpska, Mr. Jovo Rosic. Do you remember him being there at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he was at that meeting or not, but I know that Mr. Rosic came to the area of Odzak municipality. When exactly, I can't say right now, because I really don't know. I know that he was present and that he held certain talks, but whether on that day or on a different day, probably, perhaps, this Mr. Ratomir provided information which said that we were all there on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of this dispatch, Colonel Simic, the commander of the Tactical Group 1, says that on the 11th of May, which means the day before this dispatch was written, Minister Borivoje Sendic also arrived in Odzak, who I suppose was the minister for forestry. Do you remember perhaps whether this minister was also present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these leaders who came mostly spoke to the command of the Tactical Group, so if he was there, he was probably in touch with him. I know that these people came and went, and now as far as the precise date, I find that very difficult to say whether it was a day sooner or a day later. I really can't be very specific about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Finally, please, tell us the following: Concerning the level of these participants and their positions, you personally, or Dr. Simic, as the president of the War Presidency in Samac, were you in a position in any way to influence the relationship between the military administration and the government of Republika Srpska or the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, before he answers that, I'd object. It's outside the scope of cross-examination. I never questioned him concerning the influence of the Crisis Staff over the republic of Srpska or the relationship of the military and the government. That's totally outside. He brought that up in direct examination and I never got into any of that in cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It came, Your Honour, from the exhibit P169, which was tendered into the evidence just this morning. And since the persons that I just mentioned were present, according to this information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- on page 1, normally I'm asking his personal knowledge about the influence of the local organs with the government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. When you come to asking whether people were present and whether or not this institution had any influence, that's a totally different question, and as the Prosecution says, it wasn't raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can be more specific for this particular meeting. So in that term, maybe I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, not even for this particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovic, tell me: I'm really sorry to have to ask you the following line of questions to you. This is something which the Prosecutor forced me to do by asking you a series of questions in relation to your personal credibility. These questions refer to the SDS, the SDS policies, Biljana Plavsic, and so on and so forth. So I must ask you the following now, since this has been broached by the Prosecution: Tell me, the platform and the policies of the SDS, how would you characterise them or describe them? Briefly.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original platform or programme of the SDS, as concerns that, I said at the beginning that I had been a member of the League of Communists. I am a leftist by conviction, a democrat. Some parts of that platform, and with other friends of mine and colleagues, we found certain possibilities. This platform that was offered in the space and at the time was acceptable in some way because you could see that the general population, not because Karadzic or Mladic or anyone else was concerned, came, approached, since there were national tensions caused by Croats and Muslims. It was only normal to expect that such activity and such a platform people would take sides, on the basis of the platform or, rather, accept or acknowledge certain elements espoused by the platform, the policies. And therefore, I was in a position, as a man who was in some way involved in politics, to accept part of the platform that could have been some sort of a platform for activity of us leftists in the overall state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, please tell me: Was the SDS ever banned from their activity by any part of the international community?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was never banned, but I know that memberships were frozen at a certain point in time and all activity was frozen as concerns that political party during a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In order to avoid any misunderstanding, this freezing of activity, who was it ordered by and in which period specifically, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was towards the end of 1992, but I'm not sure. I know that for a period of time, all activity was stopped on the part of the SDS. I'm not sure. I know that this was referred to. But as I was not a member, I know that it was in that period; whether 1992 or 1993, it was said that no party activity should be pursued during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean it was a decision taken by the SDS themselves, as an organisation?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please: The current president of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which party is he a member of, Mr. Sarovic? Which party does he belong to?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object. That's outside the scope of our indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. We are not dealing with current affairs, are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, not directly, but since the position of the Prosecution is that the membership in SDS party is something which is wrong, which is to some extent might be a criminal act, that's why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's no such --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's my impression, Your Honour. That's my impression of the line of the questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is wrong. There's no such allegation by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean not allegations directly, but my conclusion is -- was that maybe I'm wrong. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with the SDS, tell me, please: You, as the -- that was the question asked by the Prosecution. They asked you about instructions coming from high on, from higher levels of the SDS and then percolating downwards. The Prosecutor mentioned Biljana Plavsic's admission and her conviction. My question is: Did you personally, at any point in Samac -- can you hear me? Can you hear me, Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear the question. The line was down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fine. I'll repeat the question. You personally, Mr. Popovic, did you have any information or knowledge that in 1992 and 1993, the higher organs of the SDS issued instructions to people at the local level or to the Crisis Staff, more specifically, as to how the Crisis Staff for the War Presidency should operate? Do you have any personal information in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen any such instructions, nor has anyone informed me of anything like that. Now, whether the Executive Board or the government, as they refer to it in the municipalities, had any such instructions, and probably they did, and probably they worked pursuant to those instructions, but the Crisis Staff or, after a month or two or three, it was transformed into a War Presidency which numbered, say, three members. I'm not sure even about three members. I have never seen any such instructions, nor has anyone ever informed me of the existence of any such instructions. If there was, then it was towards the Executive Board or the executive organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have a degree in economics? You talked about the Executive Board. Were these instructions issued by the relevant ministries or were these party instructions?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These could have been certain ministries of the governments. And as far as the parties, if memberships were frozen, then I can't see why the party would have issued any such instructions if it had already frozen all of its activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were asked the same question by the Prosecutor concerning the relationship between Blagoje Simic and the higher-level bodies. In 1992 and 1993, was Blagoje Simic a member of the leadership of the SDS at the republic level? Do you have any information concerning that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any information that he was a member of the leadership or of the higher-level bodies of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, the Prosecutor asked you about the establishment and the work of the Serbian municipality of Samac and of Pelagicevo. They showed you extracts from the Official Gazette. Do you have any personal information on the existence of instructions by the Assembly of Republika Srpska for these organs at the local level not to be activated unless the vital interests of the Serbian people were jeopardised? Do you know anything about any such instruction?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't think I fully understood your question. Instructions related to what exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal information concerning the instructions or decision by the Assembly of Republika Srpska that the local assemblies would not be activated unless vital interests of the Serbian people were jeopardised? Just tell me if you know or not.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, if you know, whether in April 1992, did the municipality of Samac, Domaljevac, start working in the former municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Under whose control?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the control of the HDZ, under Croatian control.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were also asked by the Prosecutor, in terms of certain decisions by the Executive Board and some that were adopted at the Municipal Assembly of the Serbian people in Obudovac, there were certain subjects to do with the position of Stevan Todorovic, police forces, et cetera. I'm now asking you the following: Who was in command and who was the superior organ to the public security station in Samac? That's one question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that, Your Honour. There's been no cross-examination on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was when my learned friend mentioned the conclusions of the Executive Board and the tasks of the special police unit, headed by Mr. Stevan Todorovic. So in that sense, I have to clarify --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I asked him about that, but I never went into who was in authority of the MUP or the SUP. If I was given another hour and a half or two, I would have gotten into a lot of issues, but that I never went into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that there is no record. I did say that I will allow you to go ahead because the question is connected to what the Prosecution had raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Popovic, according to your knowledge, who was the superior organ, and who was in command of the police forces of the public security station in Samac? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic was under the command of the Security Services Centre in Bijeljina. As far as I know, that later became Brcko, of the Crisis Staff or the War Presidency. So in terms of vertical hierarchy, it was the Security Services Centre and the ministry. So he never asked us anything, he never reported to us, so we couldn't have asked him anything and we couldn't have influenced anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because of some technical difficulties during your answer, line 23 of page 57, 58, until line 3, there were certain things that were not logical. Mr. Popovic, can you answer very briefly: Who was superior authority of the Samac public security station and who was in the top of that hierarchy in 1992 and 1993, of the police hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public security of the station of the area, Bijeljina, and then further up would be the ministry, Ministry of the Interior of the republic. That would be then the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So this previous part of the answer, just for the record, I would like to have it stated that because of some technical difficulties, part of the answer from page 57, line 24, 25, and page 58, line 1, 2, 3, should not be taken into consideration, because there were certain technical difficulties. Thank you. Mr. Popovic, you were asked by the Prosecutor about the relationship between Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, and Simeon Simic, and whether they were related. According to your knowledge, were they close relatives or were they not close relatives?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know this place where they were born, they have the same last name, but they're not connected in terms of family. I think they're very distant relatives, so to speak. You know what close families, if these are children from two brothers or two sisters, but they are not related in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you were asked several questions by the Prosecutor about the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo, and he also mentioned the term "shadow government." Now, I have to ask you several questions about that. Can you tell me whether in that time - and we're speaking about April 1992 - was there a republic of the Serbian people established in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was in 1992. I think it was established then. That would have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether at that time, the beginning of 1992, was there a constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an accurate answer. I know it was mentioned, the constitution was mentioned, but whether it existed or not, I'm really not well informed in relation to the constitution. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether at the time there was the government of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina that was established, led by Professor Djeric? Do you recall that. Is there anything you can say about that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I know that that was the government, or at least that was presented to the public, that there was this government, and the Prime Minister was such-and-such, and there were certain ministries that existed. How much they were able to operate from the then position I occupied, I couldn't tell. I think in terms of administration and paper and red tape, everything was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, if today Republika Srpska functions as one of the entities, then can you tell me, your position, whether at that time, could you have understood it as being a shadow government, or was it a regular government? What was your position on that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering everybody worked publicly, they held meetings at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina and also on local levels, when we're talking about the establishment of Serb municipalities, Croatian municipalities, municipalities and so on, I don't think that was any kind of shadow government at all, because it was publicly stated and declared.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What's the basis for objection, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll withdraw. It's just this is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm really surprised. He explicitly take -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. What I was talking in terms of a shadow government, that they had parallel governments, he's trying to talk in terms of shadow government in terms of legitimacy of governments and because there's a valid government today pursuant to the Dayton Agreement, that therefore the fact that there was a shadow government back then it was some sort of legitimate government. We're not -- we did not discuss in cross-examination the legitimacy or the validity of the government. There was a shadow government or a parallel government established. I'm not arguing that. But he's trying to back door it into an issue based on the fact that there's a legitimate government today, therefore, do you believe that it was a legitimate government back then? And that's what they're trying to get this person to comment on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't help the case of the Defence at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Your Honour, that's a legal issue at the end of the day. I know that. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then why are you raising it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He -- because it was raised during the cross-examination, Your Honour. My learned friend asked him whether the Municipal Assembly was some sort of shadow government. So I have to clarify with this witness what is his knowledge of the term of "shadow government." So it was raised during the cross-examination, simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, can you tell me: When you were talking about Colonel Djurdjevic, can you tell me whether later on, because you're somewhat related to him in some way, he is about ten years your senior, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't believe he is older. I said he was about my age. So he was about 50 at the time, like me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, can you tell me, because you're closely related to him, do you know whether he was ill at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, from that time onwards, in the next ten years, was he sick?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He got ill some time ago and he died about a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What did he die of?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He died of cancer. He had a tumor. So that spread very quickly, and the man died very quickly. But he didn't -- there were no symptoms when he was ill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... details.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It had nothing to do with the Defence case. That's what I said sometime back that you don't imitate the mistakes of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I agree with that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you're winding up?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just a short glance on the issues, and I think I've finished with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Prosecutor showed you this morning Official Gazette about the decision on the appointment of Mitar Mitrovic as the secretary of the municipality. Do you remember that? It was signed by the acting president, Mr. Tanasic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was a decision that was published there. Do you personally know whether he, Mitrovic, was issued a ruling by the relevant organ? Just tell me if you know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished with my re-direct [In English] [Previous interpretation continues] ... questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic. You are finished your evidence. You may go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is the end of the videolink witnesses, so we go back to our normal proceedings in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask, respectfully, this Trial Chamber to allow me, let's say, around 15 minutes to prepare. Because next witness, I'm just in the middle of cross-examination of next witness, who should come, Mr. Simeunovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just to arrange some papers here. Fifteen minutes would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall take our break early, then. This is 12 -- almost 12.15. So we shall continue our proceedings at 12.45. No, no, no. This is 20 minutes. 12.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness be brought, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Simeunovic. We are continuing with you. Mr. Pantelic continues asking you questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Simeunovic. May we proceed, please. The Prosecutor asked you, on the 3rd of March, Monday, -- my mistake, sorry. My colleague Lukic asked you the question in relation to the appointment of Captain Jez as the chief of security at brigade level, and so on. You answered that you carried out certain arrests, and when you said "you," you mean the army of Republika Srpska. One of these cases was the arrest of Captain Jez at Donji Zabar. Do you remember being asked that by Mr. Lukic and then you started your answer?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I referred to the arrest --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, Mr. Simeunovic. I'm sorry to interrupt you. Let me just ask you the following: Do you remember what you said in connection with that? And then I will ask you another question. If you don't remember, because some time has passed, after all, I can read this out to you to remind you.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember stating that Captain Jez was arrested at Donji Zabar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then, in continuation of your answer, you said that he was arrested because of certain cooperation with them, meaning, I presume -- I presume that you meant Todorovic and the volunteers, and so on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So at that time when you, or rather, the competent organs of Republika Srpska, according to your personal knowledge, since Captain Jez, because of the cooperation with Todorovic and the volunteers, because he was arrested at that time, as part of the proceedings of Republika Srpska were there any proceedings that were then initiated against Todorovic and his volunteers because of their behaviour and beating of prisoners in Samac? Just tell me if you have any knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There were no proceedings that were initiated, because at that time they were not members of the Yugoslav People's Army or of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. At that time there were no proceedings initiated because of a number of murders that have been committed by Todorovic and by volunteers from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proceedings that was initiated, I know they arrested Crni and a number of volunteers after the corridor had been cut off, and they were taken to the military prison in Banja Luka. Todorovic was not arrested because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Further on, my learned colleague Mr. Weiner asked you on that day, in connection to Simo Zaric's statement, that is, 542 exhibit, P142, that is, statement of Simo Zaric, and in that statement, Mr. Zaric talks about the alleged involvement of Blagoje Simic in the act of bringing the volunteers to Samac. Do you recall when the Prosecutor quoted this to you?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me: At that time, your answer was that you had no reason to doubt the statement by Simo Zaric, because he was an intelligence officer, and today, is that the same, that you have no doubt to doubt his statement?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I have no reasons to doubt his statement, but as I said then, I know who welcomed that group of volunteers, who came to Batkusa. Blagoje was not one of them -- was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simeunovic, can you tell me: Considering that the Prosecutor quoted you Zaric's statement, where he said that he had certain -- there were certain indications according to Zaric that Dr. Simic was involved in the act of bringing these volunteers, and you agreed with that. Did you ever receive from Simo Zaric, as from your subordinate intelligence officer, a report about a possible role of Blagoje Simic in the act of bringing the volunteers? Did you get a report or a dispatch from him? Do you know what I mean? Have you received anything like that from him?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that after Simo Zaric arrived, when he went to Belgrade to forward what had happened in Crkvina and to ask for some kind of protection, I know what he said at the time when he returned, when he was reporting to the Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic. He said that he found out there that from the Samac government, there was a possibility that was asked from Samac, from RV PVO to transfer those volunteers to the Samac municipality, that he had seen such a request that was submitted by the government of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. When I now read to you statement of Simo Zaric, you can then give your assessment, of course. That's page 56 of his statement dated 1st of April, 1992 -- 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And he says -- he was asked by Mrs. Nancy Paterson: "Did you ask Mr. Zaric about the role and where these volunteers have come from?" And Simo Zaric then says to the investigators of the Tribunal the following: "Yes, but this true information I found out only in the course of the war. They were in a completely different area of responsibility. It was there in the village of Batkusa where there was a completely different detachment. I was linked to the town of Samac. I later found out that they came, organised by the command of RV PVO of the army of Yugoslavia. It was their organisation, in their security service of that command. It was the command of RV PVO of Yugoslavia, which was the joint link with some representatives of the Serbian MUP. Yes, there was that connection. I think that that's how it happened, through that connection, that there was RV PVO security and the security of the Serbian MUP. I know that from finding out about it later. That's how it arrived, through that line. And Stevan Todorovic was the link that brought these people to the territory of Samac." You have no reason to doubt Mr. Zaric's words?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Further on, you were asked by the Prosecutor about the meeting in Donji Zabar which was organised by Nikolic. Can you tell me, Mr. Simeunovic -- let me remind you: This is about certain gathering between the civilian authorities and the commander Nikolic, and according to you, he then later informed, and so on. You were asked by the Prosecutor. Now I'm asking you: Do you have any knowledge whether Commander Nikolic invited to that meeting representatives of the other two ethnic groups, Muslims and Croats, specifically? Did he also invite them, considering that you mentioned civilian authority? Do you have such knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any such knowledge. He didn't mention that he invited others to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was at the time the president of the municipality of Municipal Assembly of Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I knew --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you: Mato Lujic.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know he was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You also testified that Commander Nikolic, together with the chief of police, Dragan Lukac, had joined patrols, checkpoints. Do you remember at those checkpoints that were set up? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Did Nikolic invite Dragan Lukac to this meeting with the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't invite him, and I don't see the reason why he should have invited him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. At that time you said -- or you answered to the Prosecutor that it was said that the volunteers will be under the command of the civilian authorities, not under the command of the army, because they were not members of the JNA, they were not part of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They showed official IDs that showed that they were members of the police of Serbian Krajina. As such, they could not have been under the command of the army, of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In his interview, Simo Zaric, in his interview dated 1st of April, 1998, on page 55, in relation to Commander Nikolic, he says: "Since the commander said that he would put them under his control, and he was also my commander, it wasn't up to me to do anything more than that." You have no reason to doubt these words. This is correct, what he said in his interview, Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it's true what Simo said, but the commander could not have placed them under his command, because they were not members of the Yugoslav People's Army. Perhaps in some conversation or other he may have said: I'll try and place them under my command. But later on, after their arrival, and after reporting the Superior Command, there was this meeting in Donji Zabar that happened, the one that we already spoke about, and he said -- and that's when he was told who were these people, under whose authority they were, and he said that he had no authority, nor could he place them under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to my learned colleague. Just to avoid any misunderstanding. When quoting the interview of Mr. Zaric, it was quite obvious that Mr. Zaric used the word "under control." To put these men under control. This doesn't mean -- it doesn't have same meaning as under command. So basically, I just want to avoid any misunderstanding of what the witness answered. I could wait for re-direct, but it's quite obvious what ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will continue to quote from page 54 of the same interview by Simo Zaric: "Nikolic told us that the command then, that it was some kind of a gang, meaning the volunteers, and that we will see what will happen to them, as it says here, and that he will deal with them, and so on. After a few days, he then gave information that he would place them under his control and that we shouldn't worry about this at all." You have no reason to doubt Simo Zaric's words? Let's just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. You can explain that to the -- to my colleague. Now, can you tell me: You were asked by the Prosecutor about Mico Ivanovic, Mijak. You had information that Mico Ivanovic, Mijak, was appointed as the commander of the Territorial Defence. Can you just confirm this: That man, Mico Ivanovic, Mijak, at that time, he had a dual function. He was the commander of the 1st Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group, at the same time he was the commander of the TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the commander of the 1st Detachment, and we received a piece of information saying that he had been proposed to become the commander of the TO, that if this becomes established, that he would be the commander of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me: When did you find that out, you personally?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was immediately before this group arrived, so this was in early April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, Mr. Simeunovic: At the time, did you have any personal knowledge about the establishment of MUP of Republika Srpska? I'm talking about April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand. Which MUP do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Serbian MUP, the MUP of Republika Srpska, Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, in March/April 1992. Mico Stanisic, Momcilo Mandic, going all the way up. You know what I mean. You know what I'm talking about. Have you had any intelligence about that, that the Serbian MUP had been established?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me something else: You were also asked by the Prosecutor about whether you knew that Stevan Todorovic was establishing a police unit, et cetera, and you later said that this group of 23 young men had returned from training and that it was then that you found out that Todorovic was establishing this. And then you were further asked by the Prosecutor whether you knew about the fact that Todorovic had been ordered, either by the Municipal Assembly or the Crisis Staff, even before the war, to establish these units. And then you said that probably somebody was issuing orders to him and that this was the Crisis Staff that was doing this. Now, I'm asking you, and that the Crisis Staff didn't have any cooperation with the JNA. Now, my question is: In case that the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska had been established at the time, who would have been superior? Who would have been the superior organ to the public security station and Stevo Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The witness has just testified that he wasn't aware that the -- of the establishment of the Ministry of Interior of the Republika Srpska. And now he's asking about an agency that he wasn't aware was established, who would be superior, or if it would be superior - I'm sorry - to the SUP in Samac. You can ask him -- it's almost a legal question. If it has been established. Or it's a governmental question. Would it -- would they have been superior. But based on his previous testimony, I think it's not admissible at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's beyond what factual knowledge the witness would be able to give evidence on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simeunovic, you are a man who dealt with problems of military security. You probably know something about civilian security as well. Can you tell me: In April, May, June of 1992, who was, organisationally speaking, above public security station in Samac? Do you have any later knowledge or do you have any contemporaneous knowledge about that? It's a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above the station in Samac, there should have been a unit. Now, whether this is on the principle of a region, whether this was a MUP which coordinated these stations in the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And above that regional level, who was that?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then it would be the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you say "republic," you mean Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Inaudible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the answer. Can the witness repeat the last answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When I said republic, you meant Republika Srpska. Can you just say it audibly so that it's on the record, please.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about that period now, that the station of police was established and it was a Serbian station in Serbian Samac, then, as far as the region that encompasses is concerned, under the control of Serbia [as interpreted] then it would -- that would be under the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one small correction. On page 73, line 6, under the control, it didn't say Serbia of Serbs, because Serbia is another state, and simply it would just imply something different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Thanks to my colleague Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simeunovic, we're talking about those young men from the surrounding villages of Samac municipality who were sent for training. Did you know that they were leaving, that they were being sent to training?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't know. We only learned, when they arrived by helicopters. It was only then that we learned that about 23 of them had left and that Aco Jankovic from Batkusa was their commander. He was the leader of the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You said a minute ago, that's in your previous testimony, that you would receive daily reports, daily information, from your subordinates, from your colleagues from the detachment concerning the security situation. You do remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. Except for the 1st Detachment, we never received even a regular report, let alone interim reports, from the 1st Detachment. No such reports from the 1st Detachment ever reached the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry to interrupt. As a matter of clarity, it says, they asked about the -- this group that was sent for training and it says: "We didn't know. We only learned when they arrived by helicopters. It was only then that we learned." Is he referring to the JNA command, the JNA, he and members of his unit? I think it's important that we know who he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simeunovic, please, when you say "we," or "you," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant is that I found out then, and immediately after I had learned that, I told Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic about it. As a command, we found out on that day that they had left and been sent for training. We didn't know at that point, but later we found out that the training had taken place in Sarengrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which means soldiers are being sent for training, and you, as the superior security body, didn't know about that; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. And I did say that. The detachment, upon its establishment, had no barracks. I told you this about the 4th Detachment, but the same applied to all the other detachments. Those people were assigned to the detachment. They received weapons, but they were at their homes. They went about their business or they travelled. They would be away for five, ten days, a month, and they had no obligation to report to the commander of the detachment. They were free -- well, in a manner of speaking. They were citizens doing their duty. Only he was in the records of the detachment, his name was. And that's why we didn't know that those people had actually left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand, people received mobilisation call-ups, they would place themselves under the command of the 17th Tactical Group. Were they free to move about or did they have to ask permission by the organs of the 17th Tactical Group? How did that really work in practice?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until [as interpreted] the outbreak of hostilities, the 17th, the 18th, and onwards, they did have to ask for permission, but prior to that point, they were free to travel wherever they wanted to. They weren't supposed to report to anyone. They weren't even supposed to report to their own detachment commander if they wanted to leave for five or ten days, to do something for themselves. They were people with seasonal jobs in different places.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There is just one word here that makes a complete sense [sic] of this part of the testimony. On page 75, line 12. It's not "until," but after the outbreak of hostilities. And now it makes sense what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that will be corrected. Mr. Pantelic, you have had enough time for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will cover just a couple of more issues, variant A and B, particularly, then some reports to the Superior Command, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Those are not matters peculiar to the defence of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They are general.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. They are very specific, because this witness mentioned some organs, like Crisis Staff or, namely, my client, with certain activities regarding volunteers. So I'm just specific to the role of my client and the institution where he was head of. For example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you wind up -- so I'll give you 15 minutes, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you send to your Superior Command, to the corps, the 17th, commanded by General Savo Jankovic, did you send a report regarding volunteers who had arrived back from their training? Did you report to your Superior Command?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, I was present when they arrived in the village of Batkusa. After that, I went straight to the command and reported to Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic. He called, as I said, the Superior Command immediately and asked them whether they knew who the people were who had arrived by helicopters. And he received no reply from them. He didn't know who the people were. He said a meeting would take place, and then a meeting took place in order to find out who the people were who had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In connection with this issue, because you were asked by the Prosecutor and you referred to the TO, tell me: Who commands a unit of the TO? The civilian government, that is, the municipality, or the superior military command? Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Previously, the TO was commanded by the Yugoslav People's Army, the Yugoslav People's Army commanded previously. But if we're talking about Mijak, who was appointed commander of the TO, the JNA did not appoint him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's beyond dispute. That's regulated by the statute of the municipality. That means until the 19th of May - that's when Colonel Lieutenant Nikolic withdrew - the JNA commanded the TO, to all intents and purposes?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Effectively, there was no TO. That was under the command of the JNA. The people who were there who were assigned to the TO reported to detachments that had been established by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, concerning Blagoje Simic, you were shown by the Prosecutor the Official Gazette, P124, Exhibit number P124. The question was whether you knew about -- actually, this was never shown to you. You were just simply asked whether you knew that the municipal board of the SDS had initiated the appointment of Blagoje Simic as president of the assembly and later as president of the Crisis Staff. This is clear enough, the way it's stated in the Official Gazette. Do you know that at that time, the president of the Serbian municipality, at first, was Ilija Ristic and was then replaced by Dusan Stanisic? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember at all having been asked about the Official Gazette of the Municipal Assembly. I don't remember at all this being referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I'm asking you: Do you remember that the president of the Serbian municipality was Ilija Ristic at that time and was then to be replaced by Dusan Stanisic, please answer if you know? If not, not.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I was an intelligence officer, but I was not in a position to know everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But did you know about this specifically?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Dusan Tanasic was the president of the SDS in Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was appointed president of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, you were asked by the Prosecution, and you answered that you were pro Yugoslav, that you were a Yugoslav by conviction, and that this was the idea you advocated. At that time, were you in favour of protecting the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina by remaining within Yugoslavia? Was that your line of thinking in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had Bosnia-Herzegovina remained part of Yugoslavia and the Serbian people in it, there would have been nothing to protect it from. We would have remained within Yugoslavia, as had been the case up to that point. What we advocated was for Bosnia-Herzegovina to remain within Yugoslavia, as had been the case up to that time. That's the idea we advocated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the plebiscite of the Serbian people at the end of 1991? The question was: Do you wish to stay within Yugoslavia or do you want an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina? Do you remember or not?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You did take part in the plebiscite, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At that time, the end of 1991 until April 1992, were you in favour of an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina or did you wish Bosnia-Herzegovina to remain within Yugoslavia? Because it's not quite clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is outside the scope of my cross-examination. How is this relevant, his personal views on Bosnia-Herzegovina? It's one thing if it's the JNA views or the command of the JNA, but it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's relevant, Your Honour, first of all on page 36 on the transcript of the Monday, 3rd of March, he was asked by the Prosecution: What is your convictions there, whether you were in favour of the separate, allegedly separate actions of the SDS and stuff like that. First of all, the line of questioning is related to some extent to the credibility of this witness, and then to clarify his position, because it is not clear from his answer on Monday, 3rd of March, whether he's speaking prior to April 16 or after. Simple as that. I just want to clarify that. And I'm leaving this topic, because I got the answers from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Simple as that. Could we have Exhibit P100, P100.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Furthermore, you were asked by the Prosecutor, in detail, about Biljana Plavsic's admission. Tell me, please, first of all,

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMEUNOVIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the Samac level, the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can I take a look, please? Your Honour, I do apologise. There are some problems in my list of -- it's P3, actually, Mr. Usher. I do apologise. Because it's a variant A and B, and there are many numbers of the documents, so it was not so clear here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, Mr. Simeunovic, before the document reaches you, please tell me: What's your personal knowledge - I'm talking about the period in late 1991 and the outbreak of hostilities in April 1992 - your personal information regarding the relationship between the SDS and the JNA in the Samac municipal area? How would you describe that? Was there any cooperation? Were there any plans? Please tell me briefly so we can start with the document.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was cooperation at some level. It was not totally rejected. Everything would be debated. Talks would be held for conflict to be dealt with in a peaceful manner, to keep hostilities from breaking out. That sort of cooperation took place, not only on the part of the SDS, but the other parties too. They tried everything possible to avoid conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. In Samac, in late 1991 and until April 1992, did the JNA make any secret plans with the SDS concerning the takeover of power in setting up organs of Serb government?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you now have a look at the document in front of you. It has several pages. Can you please leaf through them. Just briefly: This document allegedly speaks about -- but we don't know if it's a document or a paper, actually, speaks about the cooperation between the SDS and the JNA. There are two possible scenarios, where the Serbian deputies in the local assembly are in the majority, and the other scenario is where the Serbian deputies are in the minority. And it talks about cooperation with the JNA. First of all, my question is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. Your Honour, this is a complicated document. It's several pages long. It's eight pages long. If you're going to question this witness concerning that document, he should be entitled to read the document or at least go through it, not look at it for 30 seconds and then start questioning him on it. That's not fair to the witness, it's not fair to the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will establish just right now personal knowledge of this witness with regard to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Simeunovic: You've looked at the title, you've looked through the document. Can you please have a look at the last page. This document, in this form, did you see it while you held the position of the head of security in the 17th Tactical Group and other units later on? Have you ever seen this document up to now?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never laid eyes on this document, and I would really have to go through it thoroughly in order to be able to discuss it. This last page is illegible. It's a very poor copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We're not going to go into that now, Mr. Simeunovic, and we can't, for the simple reason that you've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But in this document, all I can see is the title, "The Serbian Democratic Party of the Serbian municipality, Main Board."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the area of Samac municipality, as you held those positions, did you ever see a document like this in this form and with this title?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were asked by my learned friend, friend and colleague, Mr. Weiner, in connection with the special battalion, as part of the 17th Tactical Group, special battalion. Can you remember: When was it set up? Late April 1992 perhaps. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special battalion was set up not late April. It wasn't even there in May. It wasn't around. It was later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just tell us, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps early May, after the JNA left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were asked by the Prosecutor about Mrs. Biljana Plavsic's view on the shadow government, about her statement, her view, and Simo Zaric's view. What I want to know, more specifically, is the following: The SDS, to the best of your knowledge --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I never asked him -- I never asked the witness about his -- Biljana Plavsic's view. I asked him about the instructions that Biljana Plavsic and the SDS and Serb leaders issued to the municipalities, not their view; the instructions from the top that they issued down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. The Prosecution is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I'm about to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal information whether the SDS sent any military instructions from the top down to their own organs at the municipal level? Did they deal with military issues, according to your information?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The SDS organs at the republic level, did they forward military instructions to their own bodies at the municipal level? I'm not talking about Samac, only specifically. Do you know anything about things like those happening?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say, because I did not attend any of those top-level meetings. I can't tell you whether they sent anything to the municipal boards. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm merely trying to find out the following, the extent of your personal knowledge concerning the local level. Did you hear that the SDS ever received any military instructions or instructions of a military nature? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Finally, I have one or two questions left. Which day is the day of the feast day of the Samac municipality, traditionally?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the 16th of April now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, you were asked by the Prosecution, quoting Biljana Plavsic, talking about different acts that are viewed as persecution, or classified as persecution. There's a concept there, but I must ask you first of all if you understood what you were asked, to begin with. The Prosecutor said that Biljana Plavsic had pleaded guilty to crimes of persecution, saying that Biljana Plavsic and members of the Bosnian Serb forces, Bosnian Serb politicians and government organs, and their agents, this word, "agent," that's the word that the Prosecutor suggested to you. I'm not sure if you know what's meant by this concept. Do you know that the army of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't really remember the word being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to say: Once again, these aren't my words. He -- counsel constantly takes all of these questions out of context. If he's going to ask him about a question that he was previously -- which is previously stated by the Prosecutor, he should read that particular question, as opposed to just making some summary and taking it all out of context. That was a comment from Biljana Plavsic as part of her plea, that she, the leadership of the Serb government, the SDS, the remaining leadership, the subgovernment units and their agents committed persecution, or actually, orchestrated a campaign of persecution against the non-Serb public of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's not my comment; that's Biljana Plavsic, one of the Serb leaders, comments or admissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The time is up, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I just clarify that submission of my learned friend with the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will read this portion. It's page 49 of LiveNote version of the transcript of March 3rd. The Prosecution just makes some references to the Biljana Plavsic and my learned friend stated: "Are you aware --" that was a question to this witness: "Are you aware that Biljana Plavsic has pled guilty to the crime of persecutions, indicating that she and members of the Bosnian Serb forces, Bosnian Serb political and government organs, and their agents, committed five of those acts that I just read to you? Were you aware that --" et cetera, et cetera. The answer of this witness was: "I'm aware that Biljana Plavsic confessed her guilt. Perhaps the reporting was not very detailed in our part of the world, but they did say that Biljana Plavsic had confessed to her guilt and that is why this judgement was passed upon her."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So now -- [Interpretation] Now, my question to you is this: Do you know that the theory of the Prosecution at this Tribunal is that the army of the Republika Srpska was actually just an agent of the JNA? Do you know about this theory?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that, Your Honour. That's been a finding in the Krstic case, it's been a finding in the Tadic case. It has been the theory of the Prosecution, but it has also been finding by the Courts of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the question is taking us nowhere, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just want to clarify with this witness the relation on Samac municipality, within organs of JNA and local politicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then ask a direct question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But first I would like to introduce a witness with the term of "agent," because he was probably misled by certain references that my learned friend made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Simeunovic, my question is: According to your information, to your personal and professional information, as a man who headed a security body, in Samac municipality, was there any plan or any cooperation between members of the JNA, on the one hand, and members of the local organs of the SDS, on the other, concerning the takeover by force or any crimes that were committed?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were meetings, but I don't know that there was ever any discussion of the JNA taking part in the takeover of power. Meetings were held with the SDS, with the SDA, and with the HDZ, with the aim of preventing bloodshed. The aim was to protect the civilian population, to protect the area. Meetings were held for that purpose only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As opposed to making plans for the takeover of power?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of any such plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My last question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic -- no, no, no. Sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You've taken your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Time is time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It won't take long. I can promise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Simeunovic. Considering that I was present during the main part of your examination, I will just have a very short time, stemming from the questions that were asked both by the Prosecutor and by Mr. Pantelic. These are only some slight clarifications in respect of things you have already spoken about here. First of all, when you were asked by Mr. Pantelic about raising of combat readiness of the detachment, he always used the date 16th of April. So now I'd like you to tell us: When you spoke about that, that the commander had decided to raise the combat readiness of the 4th Detachment, was it on the 16th of April or the next day, the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 17th of -- of the 4th Detachment, as well as all the other detachments, they were all issued orders to raise combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this has now been clarified, when this order was issued. Then Mr. Pantelic quoted certain parts from Mr. Zaric's book, and of course asked you if you agreed with the assessment given by Mr. Zaric, and this was in relation to the transfer of prisoners from the TO building to the military barracks in Brcko. I will now quote several more details from Mr. Zaric's book. So on page 243, first paragraph, item 6 says: "Mr. Zaric, in relation to this event, that these people over there will die if something is not done to improve their accommodation conditions." Do you agree with this quote from Mr. Zaric's book?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree, because when I came to transfer them, I saw what the conditions they were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 245 of the same book, where it says the following, Mr. Zaric says: "I told them that they should go to Brcko because of the further procedure, that there's a proper Detention Unit there with proper conditions and that they will get a doctor." This is the same as you have testified before this Tribunal, indeed in relation from Mr. Zaric's book?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just another detail from page 245, where Mr. Zaric says: "I knew whatever they were up against, they would be better off rather than being close at hand to those who were constantly assaulting them." Does this correspond to your personal knowledge as to the reasons why these prisoners were transferred from the Territorial Defence building to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. There were a number of questions in relation to what was undertaken by the relevant command of the JNA, not that this was something that was directed at you, but there was a question whether you had filed charges after you found out that Lugar had killed 16 people in Crkvina. Let us analyse this. So far it has not been contested that this has happened on the 7th or the 8th of May, on the 7th or the 8th of May in Crkvina, uncontestably the JNA still exists and is in the territory of Samac municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether Lugar was a member of the JNA at that time?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does the JNA have authority only over its own members or over people who are not its members?

utterances.speaker: MAKSIM SIMEUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It only has authority over the members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before this Trial Chamber, Stevan Todorovic -- no. In this Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
